verdict.rationale: Cloud Functions for Firebase automatically runs backend code in response to events, including Firebase Authentication and Cloud Storage triggers. However, the automation is defined by writing and deploying code rather than declarative rules. Firebase Security Rules only control data access and do not trigger actions, so they are not credited. Missing for 10: a declarative or no-code rule definition for event-triggered actions, documentation of trigger configuration depth (filters, conditions, action types), and independent or hands-on corroboration of event-trigger automation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Cloud Functions for Firebase is a serverless framework that lets you automatically run backend code in response to events triggered by background events, HTTPS requests, the Admin SDK, or Cloud Scheduler jobs.
The functions you write can respond to events generated by various Firebase and Google Cloud features, from Firebase Authentication triggers to Cloud Storage Triggers.
